criteria.criterion: `gate_enabled` returns a three-valued result distinguishing enabled / disabled / config-unreadable; no caller that needs the distinction can conflate the latter two.

AMENDED (was: fail CLOSED on unreadable): SUPERSEDED by the documented fail-open contract — `docs/plan-review-gate.md` records that an unreadable config fails an opt-in gate OFF with a warning and never auto-enables; the unreadable condition is now surfaced (distinct `unreadable` verdict + single stderr warning, never silent) rather than swallowed.

A held-out test seeds an unreadable config and asserts the gate does NOT silently disable — demonstrated RED before the fix; re-run green at close (tests/unit/test_gate_state_tristate_f5c4.py, 4 passed).

AMENDED (was: no caller relying on bool truthiness): landed design DELIBERATELY preserves `GateState.__bool__` compatibility; gates.py:213 handles tri-state explicitly; gates.py:308 and close_precheck.py:563 rely on preserved bool compat.
Existing gate on/off behaviour is unchanged for readable configs (the invariance-guard test passed pre-fix and post-fix; the change merged with Verified +1 CI, existing tests unmodified).
Bug 'gate_enabled fails OPEN and collapses gate-off with config-unreadable' is actually resolved: the reported defect no longer reproduces and expected behavior holds.
